'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Gaza war|Israel–Hamas war]]
**[[Gaza war hostage crisis|Israel–Hamas war hostage crisis]]
***[[Minister of Foreign Affairs (Tanzania)|Tanzanian Foreign Minister]] [[January Makamba]] confirms that a 21-year-old [[Tanzania]]n student was "killed immediately after being captured by [[Hamas]]" [[October 7 attacks|on 7 October]]. [https://www.newvision.co.ug/category/news/tanzania-confirms-death-of-student-captured-b-NV_176954 (AFP via ''New Vision'')]
**[[International reactions to the Gaza war|International reactions to the Israel–Hamas war]]
***[[2023 Danish terror plot]]
****Seven people are arrested in [[Denmark]], [[Germany]], and the [[Netherlands]] after police discover possible [[terrorist]] plans to attack [[Jewish]] institutions in Europe. Four of the detained are identified as [[Hamas]] members by police, a claim which Hamas has denied. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/copenhagen-police-danish-intelligence-make-arrests-suspicion-preparations-attack-2023-12-14/ (Reuters)]
*[[Sistan and Baluchestan insurgency]]
**[[Jaish ul-Adl]] [[militant]]s attack a [[police station]] in [[Rask, Iran|Rask]], [[Sistan and Baluchestan province]], [[Iran]], killing eleven officers and wounding others. Several gunmen are also killed in the ensuing [[shootout]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/baluch-militants-attack-iran-police-station-killing-11-state-tv-2023-12-15/ (Reuters)]
*[[Russo-Ukrainian war]]
**[[Russian strikes against Ukrainian infrastructure (2022–present)|Russian strikes against infrastructure]]
***[[Romania]] says that a [[Russian Armed Forces|Russian]] [[unmanned combat aerial vehicle|drone]] has crashed in its territory, leaving a [[crater]] in [[Grindu, Tulcea]], near the [[Romania–Ukraine border|Ukrainian border]]. [[Romanian Air Force]] [[General Dynamics F-16 Fighting Falcon|F-16s]] and [[German Air Force]] [[Eurofighter Typhoon]]s conducted joint patrols in response to the violation of [[NATO]] airspace. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/romania-finds-drone-crater-after-russian-attack-ukrainian-infrastructure-2023-12-14/ (Reuters)]
*[[Yemeni Crisis (2011–present)|Yemeni Crisis]]
**[[Red Sea crisis]]
***[[Maersk]] calls for "political action" after a [[ballistic missile]] launched by the [[Houthi movement|Houthis]] in [[Yemen]] narrowly misses one of their [[container ship]]s in the [[Bab-el-Mandeb]] strait. An unknown vessel claiming to be from the [[Yemeni Navy]] also ordered the ship to sail towards the Yemeni coast. [https://www.thedrive.com/the-war-zone/maersk-demands-political-action-after-another-houthi-attack-on-ship-in-red-sea (The Drive)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Visa policy of Iran]]
**[[Government of Iran|Iran]] lifts [[travel visa]] requirements for [[tourism in Iran|tourists]] in 33 countries, including all [[Arab states of the Persian Gulf|Gulf states]] and one [[European Union|EU]] member state, [[Croatia]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/iran-lifts-visa-rules-33-countries-including-gulf-states-isna-2023-12-14/ (Reuters)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2023 Beijing Subway collision]]
**At least 515 people are injured in a [[rear-end collision]] between [[railroad car]]s on the [[Changping line]] of the [[Beijing Subway]] in [[China]] near the [[Xi'erqi station]] amid [[snow]]fall. [https://www.1news.co.nz/2023/12/15/over-500-people-injured-in-beijing-train-collision-amid-heavy-snow/ (AP via ''1News'')]

'''International relations'''
*[[2023 Guayana Esequiba crisis]]
**[[President of Venezuela|Venezuelan President]] [[Nicolás Maduro]] and [[President of Guyana|Guyanese President]] [[Irfaan Ali]] hold talks in [[Kingstown]], [[Saint Vincent and the Grenadines]]. Both leaders agree to use neither threats nor force against the other. A joint commission is announced to address the existing issues, with a report expected within three months. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/venezuela-guyana-presidents-meet-amid-territorial-dispute-2023-12-14/ (Reuters)] [https://apnews.com/article/guyana-venezuela-essequibo-meeting-st-vincent-173eef85a1ebe8cfaa9f1656ce3dcbd6 (AP)]
*[[2023 Nigerien crisis]]
**[[Minister of Foreign Affairs (Togo)|Togolese Foreign Minister]] [[Robert Dussey]] announces an agreement with the [[National Council for the Safeguard of the Homeland|Nigerien military junta]] for the [[Niger|country]]'s transition to [[civilian]] rule, ready for presentation to the [[ECOWAS]] with the aim of lifting Niger's suspension from the body. [https://www.thehindu.com/news/international/niger-coup-leaders-agree-to-transition-terms-togo-mediator/article67640819.ece (AFP via ''The Hindu'')]
*[[Bulgaria–Russia relations]]
**[[Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Russia)|Russian Foreign Ministry]] spokesperson [[Maria Zakharova]] says that [[Bulgaria]] will "fully pay the consequences" of its "shameful decision" to remove the [[Soviet Union|Soviet]]-era [[Monument to the Soviet Army, Sofia|Monument to the Soviet Army]] in [[Sofia]]. [https://www.express.co.uk/news/world/1845479/bulgaria-soviet-statue-demolition-russia-eu (''The Daily Express'')]
*[[Finland–United States relations]]
**[[Finland]] announces the creation of a defense cooperation agreement with the [[United States]]. The agreement will grant Finland access to [[American military]] resources for use in defensive operations, while the US will gain military access to Finland in the event of conflict. [https://www.reuters.com/world/finland-sign-defence-pact-with-us-2023-12-14/ (Reuters)]
*[[Potential enlargement of the European Union]]
**[[Accession of Ukraine to the European Union]], [[Accession of Moldova to the European Union]], [[Accession of Georgia to the European Union]]
***The EU announces the opening of accession talks with [[Moldova]] and [[Ukraine]] and the granting of candidate status to [[Georgia (country)|Georgia]]. [https://www.euronews.com/my-europe/2023/12/14/eu-greenlights-accession-talks-with-ukraine-and-moldova (Euronews)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Bloody Sunday (1972)|Bloody Sunday]]
**A former [[United Kingdom|British]] [[Parachute Regiment (United Kingdom)|paratrooper]] will stand trial in the killing of two [[civil rights]] protesters during a [[massacre]], where [[British Army|British soldier]]s shot 13 protesters during a [[protest march]] in the [[Bogside]] area of [[Derry]], [[Northern Ireland]]. [https://apnews.com/article/british-soldier-trial-killings-bloody-sunday-e1d0cb91def62e7159eeff6b61758c1f (AP)]
*[[Disappearance of Alex Batty]]
**Alex Batty, a British boy who went missing in [[Spain]] in 2017 when he was 11, is found alive in [[France]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-67718158 (BBC News)]
*A [[United States]] [[United States Navy|Navy]] officer, [[Ridge Alkonis]], jailed in [[Japan]] after being found guilty of the [[Reckless driving|negligent driving]] deaths of two local civilians, has been transferred into American custody, where he was booked into a federal detention center. [https://apnews.com/article/japan-navy-defense-department-alkonis-ca2b3de8bf962b5faa49cf4dc6bd0b88 (AP)]
*Ex-[[Federal Bureau of Investigation|FBI]] agent [[Charles McGonigal]] is [[sentence (law)|sentenced]] to over four years in prison for violating [[Countering America's Adversaries Through Sanctions Act|U.S. sanctions on Russia]], including laundering money for oligarch [[Oleg Deripaska]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-us-canada-67717790 (BBC News)]
*[[Hong Kong Police Force|Hong Kong police]] announce [[Hong Kong dollar|HK$]]1 million ([[United States dollar|US$]]128,000) [[Bounty (reward)|bounties]] for five [[2019–2020 Hong Kong protests|activists]] residing overseas, including [[Simon Cheng]], [[criminal charge|charging]] them with [[Incitement|inciting]] [[Secession in China|secession]] under the [[2020 Hong Kong national security law|national security law]]. [https://www.news18.com/world/hong-kong-offers-bounties-for-5-activists-accused-of-security-crimes-8704043.html (AFP via CNN-News18)]
*The [[New South Wales Court of Criminal Appeal]] [[acquit]]s [[Kathleen Folbigg]], overturning her 2003 [[conviction]] for the deaths of her four children, following new scientific evidence revealing rare [[genetic mutation]]s as the cause of the deaths. [https://www.ndtv.com/world-news/australian-woman-cleared-of-murder-conviction-for-deaths-of-her-4-children-4671152 (AFP via NDTV)]
*[[Online marketplace]] company [[Temu]] files a [[lawsuit]] against online fashion retailer [[Shein]], accusing Shein of "[[mafia]]-style intimidation of suppliers". [https://www.cnbc.com/2023/12/14/online-retailer-temu-files-fresh-lawsuit-against-rival-shein-in-us.html (CNBC)]
